suggestions.reason: This brief passes without ever stating that two sessions are open — the grader has to infer it from 'gate NOT ready for SES-004/SES-005' and 'SES-005 is another conversation's'. If the intent is that the second-open-session finding be explicit, require the Findings line to name the open sessions as open (e.g. 'open: SES-004, SES-005' or equivalent) so a brief that merely mentions both shas incidentally cannot pass.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' that names docs/OVERVIEW.md, CONTEXT.md and the newest SES file, and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line (a second read with offset where the tool truncated)
suggestions.reason: Two grader-judgment gaps: (1) the brief names 'OVERVIEW' not 'docs/OVERVIEW.md' — say whether shorthand basenames are acceptable, since the template's ~1,200-char budget pushes runs toward shorthand; (2) 'transcript.md shows … read to its last line' is only checkable against a self-authored summary transcript. If the harness can capture the raw tool log, grade against that; otherwise require the transcript to state each file's wc -l next to the range read so the grader can cross-check (this run did, which is why it could be verified).

The skill's own template says 'under ~1,200 characters' but the eval caps at 1,600; this brief is 1,257. Either the eval should test the skill's number (so a brief that overshoots the skill's guidance by 30% is caught) or the skill should state 1,600 — as written, a 1,599-char brief passes an eval for a skill that asks for 1,200.

No expectation checks that the brief's facts are right, only that it states them: a wrong v0.1.9 sha, a wrong unreleased range, or 'wip/visual-grouping is local' (what the docs say, but false in this clone) would all pass. This run got them right and even corrected the docs' 'local branch' claim; an expectation of the form 'the Released sha equals `git rev-parse --short v0.1.9` and the Parked line's local/remote claim matches `git branch -a`' would make that discriminating.

The template's 'Next: <item> — first step: …' label is absent from this brief (the first step is present in substance). If the template shape matters, an expectation should check the line labels; if not, the skill's 'every line present' wording is stricter than what is graded.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations pass with disk-verified evidence; the run answered the question, changed nothing, and reported the NOT-ready gate and the foreign SES-005 as findings. The expectations check presence and non-mutation well but not factual correctness of the brief's numbers, and the char cap tested (1,600) is looser than the skill's own (~1,200).
